The ranking did move well past the baseline's ceiling: roc_auc 0.9308 vs 0.9087, pr_auc 0.6135 vs 0.5645, and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.8712 vs the baseline's 0.8382 (implied KS 0.7424 vs 0.6765, i.e. +0.066 of the +0.086 the bar required). So this is not a family failure yet — but the achieved cut is off: cut_headroom 0.0446 is 82% of the remaining 0.0545, and recall 0.7382 sits 0.1768 below specificity 0.9150, which says the positive class needs *more* weight, not less. Capacity is also loose: train_balanced_accuracy 0.9775 vs val 0.8266, train_val_gap 0.1509, at 500 iterations × 63 leaves with early_stopping off, and calibration_error 0.0487 / brier 0.0743 show the probabilities are systematically off around the default 0.5 cut. Cost is not a constraint: train_time 10.5s, wall 13.1s, returncode 0, no dropped_hyperparams. Only 1 family tried so far, so no plateau evidence exists for wrong_model_family.
critic.direction: Keep hist_gbdt but push the operating point toward the balanced crossing — recall 0.7382 is well below specificity 0.9150, so raise the positive class weight from 6 to about 'balanced' (≈7.55) or 9 while trimming capacity (max_leaf_nodes 31, max_iter 300) to shrink the 0.1509 train_val_gap; this converts most of the 0.0446 cut_headroom, which is 82% of the 0.0545 still needed, without a second unattributable lever.
